This application will include: Complete Oath of Residency form, Complete Technical Standards form, Submit a resume or curriculum vitae, Valid Photo ID, Submit a $50 application fee. All applicants must possess a bachelor's degree or the equivalent from an accredited college or university prior to applying for the MPH program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness is a leading program that results in a distinctive degree. Graduates of this program will be well-prepared for the world economy of the future and will have enhanced marketability for a wide range of careers. The innovative curriculum provides a common body of knowledge for students in Agricultural Economics and Business Administration. This degree program combines core courses from Agricultural and Applied Economics with business courses in Accounting, Marketing, Management, Finance, and Business Law to provide a strong foundation for careers in management of businesses. The Agribusiness program is associated with the College of Business Administration; the curriculum includes 14 of the 17 courses required for a General Business degree from the College of Business. In addition, the curriculum includes applications courses in business finance, marketing, commodity trading analysis, real estate appraisal, international trade, and natural resource economics. An emphasis is placed on international employment opportunities with courses at the senior level in international marketing, management, and finance.

Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources Management: Conservation Science Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources Management prepares students to plan, develop, manage, and evaluate programs to protect and regulate natural habitats and renewable natural resources. All students who earn a degree in NRM will learn the science of applying ecological principles to problems in natural resources management and the art of making decisions that benefit multiple stakeholders and use our natural resources sustainably. Conservation implies a synergistic relationship between humans and the environment, and may be the most important application of ecology. It is the goal of the Department of Natural Resources Management to develop professionals with a sound understanding of ecology and skilled in the art, science, and conservation of renewable natural resource management. Conservation Science emphasizes the interdependent relationship between humans and the environment. Conservation Scientists may work with invasive species, endangered or threatened species, ecosystem restoration, or human dimensions. Graduates of this program have an unusually wide diversity of career options, most of them in the environmental arena, including environmental consulting, private industry employment, and work for the federal, state, and local governments. Many graduates also pursue further graduate studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources Management: Fisheries Biology Concentration
Description: Natural resources management in this field uses knowledge of ecological and environmental factors which affect fishes and other aquatic organisms in order to balance the growing demand on water resources with the need to maintain fisheries and ecosystem services. Careers in this field range from very applied (e.g. understanding impacts of dams on fish reproduction) to more basic research such as working on understanding the biology of a threatened or endangered species (e.g. Pecos assiminea snail). Graduates work in a variety of settings, including government agencies, consulting firms, and non-governmental organizations.
Accredidation: The fisheries biology track can meet the minimum certification requirements recommended by the American Fisheries Society for a fisheries professional.
